SUNDAY
OCTOBER 14
1 - 7 pm Activities Building
Calling all Builders! Resurrection MCC's Theatre 
department is building a set for the Lesbian landmark 
play, Last Summer at Bluefish Cove, by Jane Chambers. 
You need not be present the entire time. Whether you 
can give us an hour or the afternoon, we'd love to have 
your support! Bring your power tools or just yourself or 
some friends and let's build stuff! Light snacks will be 
provided. 
For more information, please contact Ronda Roush at 
LiturgicalTheatre@ResurrectionMCC.org or  
281-570-7774.

The prophetic liberative voices of historically oppressed communities 
  
Four speakers, a black Christian theologian, a Muslim woman activist, a Palestinian Christian 
man, and a black activist pastor come together to share about their vision of faith as a 
revolutionary space for justice based on the radical revolutionary transformative teachings of the 
prophetic. 
  
The purpose of this panel is to renew the interest and passion among activists and people of 
faith through reflection and use of the teachings of the prophetic in social justice strategies by 
 
1. Educating and activating young scholars, activists, thinkers, and doers who see the need to 
create an historical consciousness around the issue of oppression, economic subjugation, 
exploitation, and racism 
2. Understanding intersections of current struggles in communities of color  
3. Understanding the prophetic and the importance of its praxis to political struggles 
 
Reverend Ronnie C. Lister co-founded The International Center for Spiritual and 
Social Activism, along with is wife Ann.  Reverend Lister is a Public Theologian, 
Social Activist and Teacher of the relationship between spirituality and social 
justice.  Rev. Lister and his wife Ann are passionately committed to building the 
Beloved Community and the creation of a world where all people can live together 
as neighbors in God's World.   
 
 
 
 
Sobia Siddiqui served CAIR-Houston as Communications Intern in 2014. Since 
then, her work has included event planning for the annual Muslim Youth 
Leadership Symposium, organizing for Texas Muslim Capitol Day and social 
media reporting for the Texas Da’wah Convention. She has also worked with the 
Muslim American Society-Katy and the Islamic Council of North America’s Young 
Muslim Quiz Competition, all while pursuing her undergraduate education.In 2016 
Sobia spent six months teaching English to Syrian refugee families in Houston. 
 
Tarek Abuata moved from Palestine to the U.S. during the first Palestinian 
Intifada when he was 12. After graduating from the University of Texas Law 
School, Tarek started his career working for the Negotiations Support Unit of 
the Palestinian Authority, researching legal and policy issues. Since, Abuata 
worked in Palestine for eight years as the coordinator of the Christian 
Peacemaker Team, and served as the representative of Rev. Bernard 
LaFayette (protégé of Dr. King) training Palestinian youth in nonviolence 
principles and steps. Currently, Abuata serves as the Executive Director of 
Friends of Sabeel North America. 
 
Darnell Fennell serves as the pastor of Just Love. He is native Texan from 
southwest Houston. Darnell is no stranger to church having grown up in the 
Baptist tradition where he discovered a deep passion for ministry. In 2011 he 
received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and Religious Studies from the 
University of Houston followed by a Master of Divinity from Pacific School of 
Religion in Berkeley, CA in 2014. As an ordained minister in Christian Church 
(Disciples of Christ), he returned to Houston to begin work on a new church 
plant, Just Love. Darnell is over church as usual and desires to see a renewed 
Church, one that takes love seriously.

Voices of Historically

SUNDAY 
October 14 
1:30 - 3 pm • Gathering Place 
Four speakers, including Rev. Ronnie C. Lister (a black, 
Christian theologian), Sobia Siddiqui (a female, Muslim 
activist), Tarek Abuata (a male, Palestinian-Christian), 
and Darnell "D.D." Fennell (a Black, activist pastor) 
will come together to share their vision of faith as a 
revolutionary space for justice, based on the radical, 
revolutionary, and transformative teachings of the 
prophetic. The purpose of this panel is to renew 
interest and passion among activists and people of 
faith through reflection and the use of the teachings of 
the prophetic in social justice strategies.
